title: Taking turns to lead the walk
description: On a family walk, the person in front quietly makes a dozen decisions. Sharing the lead — ten minutes each, navigator's word is final — turns a stroll into a small lesson in leading and following.

body.heading: The leader's invisible job
paragraphs: The leader picks the pace, chooses at every fork, watches for traffic at crossings and decides when to stop. Followers rarely notice any of it — until they take the front and feel the gentle weight of a group trusting their choices.

Rotating the lead every ten minutes gives everyone that feeling in safe doses, children included. The rule that makes it work: during your ten minutes your route choices stand, unless safety says otherwise.

body.heading: Following is a skill too
paragraphs: The followers' job is not passive. Good followers keep the group together, call out hazards the leader cannot see, and save their better idea for their own turn at the front — a discipline some adults find harder than leading.
End the walk by naming one good decision each leader made. It closes the loop kindly, and the youngest navigator will remember the compliment far longer than the route.

takeaway: Rotate the lead every ten minutes, let each navigator's choices stand, and finish by naming one good decision each leader made.
